title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 701–703): Grothendieck is studying an extension (243) of the group (scheme) 𝔊_3, presented by two generators ρ, σ, by the constant group scheme M̲ attached to a rank-2 lattice M = Zλ0 ⊕ Zλ1. The extension is 𝔊^+/μ_𝔊, which he later calls the 'universal extension of 𝔊_3 by M'. The setting is the genus-1 / modular part of the 'Longue Marche' (Teichmüller tower, (1,1) level), though from this page alone the precise identification of 𝔊_3 is unsure.

On the previous page he fixes one splitting (ρ', σ'). The scheme Sc of splittings is then the scheme of lifts of (ρ, σ) satisfying the defining relations. It is a torsor under Sc_0, the scheme of 1-cocycles (ξ, η). By (253), Sc_0 ≅ K̲, where K = ker(Z^3 → Z, (α0, α1, β) ↦ 2α1 − α0 − 3β) ≅ Z^2.

Conjugation by a section λ of M̲ acts on Sc by (ξ, η) ↦ (ξ + (1−ρ_M)λ, η + (1−σ_M)λ). This is the coboundary map M̲ → Sc_0. On lattices it is M → K ⊂ Z^3, c0λ0 + c1λ1 ↦ (c0+c1, 2c1−c0, c1−c0).

On this page he argues as follows.
- The composite M → Z^3 is universally injective, i.e. a saturated direct summand. Indeed the 2×2 minors of its matrix are 3, 1, 2, with gcd 1.
- So M → K is universally injective between lattices of the same rank 2, hence an isomorphism 'for reasons of rank'.
- In cohomological terms, the coboundary map is an isomorphism onto the cocycles, so H^1 = 0 universally.

Proposition. The extension (243) is split over S_0. The splittings over S_0 correspond bijectively to splittings of 𝔊^+/μ_𝔊 as an abstract extension of 𝔊_3 by M. Over any base S, two splittings are conjugate by a unique section of M̲ over S. Hence the scheme of splittings is naturally an M̲-torsor, and it is trivial.

Remark. Over any S, splittings of (243) correspond to splittings of the group extension (244): 1 → M̲(S) → (𝔊^+/μ_𝔊)(S)^Δ → 𝔊_3 → 1. The next page identifies this as the pushout of the universal extension along M → M ⊗ Γ(S, O_S).

Applied to S = Spec(Ê), this gives the corollary on the next page: the completed extension is split, and its splittings form an M^-torsor. This is preparatory to classifying lifts of compatible splittings to G_{ρ,σ}/μ.

Check: the image lies in K, since 2(2c1−c0) − (c0+c1) − 3(c1−c0) = 0.
errors: Read literally, the transcription 'donc pas iso pour des questions de rang' contradicts the mathematics. M and K both have rank 2, and the map is universally injective with gcd of minors 1, so it IS an isomorphism (the proposition that follows requires this). The intended reading must be something like 'donc iso pour des questions de rang'. Either it is a mis-transcription or a slip of the pen.

ideas.what: Splittings of a group extension by a lattice form a torsor under cocycles. Conjugation by M gives the coboundary map, and showing it is an isomorphism onto the cocycle module (H^1 = 0, universally over any base) shows the splitting scheme is an M̲-torsor, here trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian H^1 / classification of complements: complements up to conjugacy ↔ H^1(G, M); scheme of sections as a torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schreier, Eilenberg–MacLane); scheme-theoretic torsor language Grothendieck/Giraud
ideas.where_published: General torsor formalism in SGA 3 / Giraud; this specific computation appears only in these Longue Marche follow-up notes as far as known

ideas.what: Integral (universal) injectivity checked via the gcd of the 2×2 minors; rank comparison then gives an isomorphism of lattices.
ideas.modern_name: Saturated sublattice / Smith normal form argument

ideas.what: Base change of the universal extension of 𝔊_3 by M along M → M ⊗ Γ(S, O_S), applied to a completed base Spec(Ê) to split the profinite/completed extension.
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of extensions; splitting of a completed (pro-)extension

deep.surprise_reason: A routine cohomological computation (vanishing of H^1 for a specific action on a rank-2 lattice) inside a longer technical development on genus-1 Teichmüller/modular group extensions. It is correct and carefully done, but contains nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'donc pas iso pour des questions de rang' should, by the mathematics, mean 'donc iso pour des questions de rang' (the map M → K is an isomorphism).
'- dans un autre sens [?] -' is uncertain; it plausibly reads as an aside meaning 'more precisely'.
'sur S_0 sur [?] Z' is plausibly 'sur S_0 = Spec Z' or similar, referring to the base S_0.
'de façon naturelle un torseur sous M̲': the crossed-out word before 'de' is illegible; the sense is 'is in a natural way an M̲-torsor'.
